title: Patty Hearst: Brainwashed or Bandit?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine whether Patty Hearst was a brainwashed kidnapping victim who was radicalized out of fear, or a willing participant in the Symbionese Liberation Army's crimes. They cover her 1974 kidnapping from Berkeley, the SLA's origins in a prison tutoring program, the food giveaway demand, her adoption of the name Tania, the Hibernia Bank robbery, the Compton house shootout, the Sunset Boulevard sporting goods shooting, her 1975 arrest and trial (with F. Lee Bailey's brainwashing defense), her sentence commutation by Jimmy Carter and pardon by Bill Clinton, and her later life including John Waters films. A listener mail segment about beavers closes the episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and the central question
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about movies and then pose the question of whether Patty Hearst was a brainwashed hostage or a willing radical.

segments.title: Hearst family and Patty's kidnapping
segments.summary: Background on the Hearst family, Patty's upbringing and life in Berkeley, and her February 1974 abduction by three SLA members who beat her fiancé Stephen Weed.

segments.title: Origins of the Symbionese Liberation Army
segments.summary: The SLA grew out of a prison tutoring program in Berkeley, with Donald DeFreeze as leader. The group was small, ideologically thin, militant, and responsible for the 1973 killing of Marcus Foster.

segments.title: Ransom demands and the food giveaway
segments.summary: The SLA's demand that the Hearsts feed poor Californians, the resulting People in Need program, and the parents' public debate over the cost of Patty's life.

segments.title: Patty becomes Tania
segments.summary: Patty's April 3 tape announcing she chose to join the SLA, her new name Tania, and the Polaroid with a machine gun and beret.

segments.title: Hibernia Bank robbery
segments.summary: The SLA robbed the Hibernia Bank in San Francisco; surveillance footage showed Patty shouting 'I am Tania' with a machine gun, which shifted public perception.

segments.title: Sporting goods store shooting and Compton shootout
segments.summary: The May 1974 sporting goods store incident in Los Angeles where Patty fired about thirty shots to cover the Harrises, the SLA hideout in Compton, and the fire that killed six members. Willie Wolfe's background is discussed.

segments.title: Life on the run, arrest, and trial
segments.summary: Patty and the Harrises fugitive period, the San Francisco bank killing of a customer, her 1975 arrest in a house with Wendy Yoshimura, and the trial where F. Lee Bailey argued brainwashing and she pleaded the Fifth.

segments.title: Sentence, commutation, pardon, and later life
segments.summary: Seven-year sentence, Jimmy Carter's commutation, Bill Clinton's 2001 pardon, her later life and John Waters films, and Kathleen Soliah's arrest.

segments.title: Listener mail: Bavarian beavers
segments.summary: A listener from Bavaria describes his civil service work with beavers and praises the show's beaver episode.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts sign off and give the contact email.
